name: Daily voucher-listing pages (/section8/)
hypothesis: The voucher feed is the only data on the site that genuinely changes daily, and 'section 8 apartments <city>' is high-volume, high-intent, commercial search. Pages that are both rebuilt daily and uniquely cross-referenced against rent-stabilized status should earn rankings that a static list cannot.
evidence: Nightly AffordableHousing.com feed already runs at 04:15 UTC; ~250 live listings match known stabilized buildings.

name: Dated daily market briefs (/brief/)
hypothesis: A dated series of real market snapshots creates a genuine archive, gives crawlers a new URL every day, and is the kind of primary source that journalists and AI answer engines cite.
evidence: Publishes only when listings actually moved, so the archive stays a data series rather than filler.

name: llms.txt + explicit AI-crawler permissions
hypothesis: AI answer engines already refer traffic (visits carry utm_source=chatgpt.com). Handing them a parseable map of the dataset, with the caveats spelled out, should increase how often we are the cited source for rent-stabilization questions.
evidence: Observed chatgpt.com referrals in the visits table before any GEO work.

name: Daily sitemap for daily-changing pages
hypothesis: The main sitemap is rebuilt monthly and would never mention today's pages. A separate daily sitemap with honest lastmod is how Google learns to re-crawl this section on a daily rhythm.
evidence: Google does not consume IndexNow; sitemap lastmod is its re-crawl signal.

name: IndexNow submission of new/changed URLs
hypothesis: 47k pages produce only ~30 organic visitors/week, which points at an indexing problem rather than a content problem. Same-day submission to Bing/Yandex/Seznam/Naver should raise the share of the corpus that is actually indexed and serving.
evidence: IndexNow key already hosted at the docroot; the existing submitter only ran on the monthly SEO rebuild, so it fired ~once a month.

name: Turn on ad inventory (AdSense)
hypothesis: Display ads across 47k pages is the lowest-effort revenue on the site, and it is currently earning exactly $0 because no ad unit is configured.
evidence: index.html sets ADSENSE_CLIENT but leaves ADSENSE_SLOT empty, and ADS_ON() requires both — so no ad script loads and no ad renders anywhere.
notes: Needs: confirm the AdSense account cleared review, create an in-feed unit, paste its slot id. One field, and inventory goes live.

name: Drive demand to the Developer API
hypothesis: Reaching $10k/mo through $4.99 consumer subs needs ~2,000 subscribers. The API reaches it with roughly 200 Pro or 50 Business customers — or a handful of Enterprise bulk licences, which is why that tier now exists. Proptech, appraisers, brokerages, tenant-side law firms and researchers all need property-level rent-regulation data and mostly cannot get it.
evidence: Verified 2026-07-26: the product is already BUILT and working end to end — self-serve signup, metered keys, live Stripe checkout (cs_live_ session confirmed), and a working webhook. The api_keys table holds only the owner's own smoke tests, so the gap is demand, not product.
notes: Enterprise tier added 2026-07-26 to raise the ceiling. REQUIRED: confirm api@findacrib.com is a live forwarding alias in Namecheap, or Enterprise enquiries bounce.

name: Daily B2B prospect research + drafted outreach
hypothesis: Nobody discovers a data API by accident, and zero real signups confirms it. A steady trickle of genuinely researched, personalised outreach converts far better than volume in markets this small.
evidence: api_keys contains no real developer signups despite the API being live since July.
notes: Drafts only, never auto-sends — bulk cold mail from findacrib.com would put the saved-building alert emails into spam, and cold outreach carries CAN-SPAM and GDPR obligations that need a human decision. Needs the Anthropic key.

name: Pitch data stories to housing reporters (earns links)
hypothesis: Domain authority is the ceiling on the 90% search-share goal, and links from housing/city desks are the highest-quality way to raise it. The daily briefs are a standing supply of original, citable findings.
evidence: Original data is the one thing reporters reliably link back to.

name: Search Console integration (measures the 90% goal)
hypothesis: We cannot steer toward 90% search share without knowing our actual positions and impressions. Search Console also exposes page-2 queries, which are the cheapest rankings to win.
evidence: seo_search_console.py is already written and working — it just has no service-account key, so it has never run.
notes: Needs: a Google Cloud service account with the Search Console API enabled, added as a user on the findacrib.com property, key stored in keychain rent-map-gsc-service-account.

name: Buyer follow-up sequence (Building Report)
hypothesis: Report buyers paid at the highest-intent moment in the funnel and each have one specific building they care about. Nudging the free DHCR rent-history request — the step that actually establishes overcharge and the easiest to put off — is useful enough to earn the open.
evidence: Free accounts were the obvious audience but only 3 have ever saved a building, too few for the 21-day review to find any signal.
notes: [2026-07-27] candidate→active: re-scoped to Building Report buyers 2026-07-27; free-account base too small to measure

name: Refresh the 'recently advertised' feed more than monthly
hypothesis: The rental-activity signal is the site's most commercial content, and it currently decays for a month between refreshes.
evidence: listings.json on the live site was last written July 1; the scrape cron runs on the 1st of the month only.

name: Neighborhood landing pages for SF / LA / DC
hypothesis: NYC has 47k pages and three other cities have one page each, so three quarters of the tracked query universe has almost no surface area.
evidence: build_seo.py is NYC-only; DC already carries real neighborhood names, so it is the cheapest of the three.

name: Rebuild the Plus upgrade funnel
hypothesis: Traffic is not the only thing between here and revenue: the current funnel has converted zero paying subscribers, so sending more traffic through it unchanged just wastes it.
evidence: subscriptions table holds 1 owner account and 5 comps — no organic paid conversions to date.

name: Dataset schema.org markup on building/neighborhood pages
hypothesis: The site's entire defensible advantage is a structured, property-level dataset almost nobody else publishes. Marking that data up explicitly as schema.org/Dataset (plus Place/Organization/GovernmentOrganization for owners and agents) gives AI systems and Google's knowledge graph a machine-readable reason to treat findacrib.com as the primary source for a specific address, not just another blue link, which matters more than ranking position for AI-answer citation.
evidence: Practitioners across the GEO category recommend a specific handful of schema types, and note that <cite index="47-11,47-12">Practitioners across the GEO category consistently recommend the same handful of schema types: Article, Organization, Product, Review, FAQPage, HowTo, QAPage, Author, Person, and Dataset.</cite> Critically, <cite index="47-16">Dataset schema is genuinely useful if you publish datasets, which most marketing sites do not.</cite> Separately, Google's own May 2026 guidance confirms <cite index="42-1">Schema.org structured data remains valuable for rich results even though no special markup is required for AI responses specifically... the effect is correlation, not causation.</cite>
notes:
effort: days
expected: Dataset/Place JSON-LD live on all 47k+ building pages within one sprint; measurable via Search Console rich-result reports and by tracking AI-referrer (utm_source=chatgpt.com/perplexity.ai) visits per week, targeting a rise from 0/day toward double digits within 60 days.
first step: Write and validate one Dataset + Place JSON-LD template against a sample of 20 NYC building pages using Google's Rich Results Test, then ship site-wide via the existing static-page generator.

name: Embeddable 'check this address' widget for reporters and tenant orgs
hypothesis: Housing reporters, tenant-union blogs, and legal-aid sites regularly need to answer 'is this building rent-stabilized' for a story or client and currently have no easy citable tool; a free embeddable widget (iframe/JS snippet) that looks up an address against the DHCR/HPD dataset turns every embed into a permanent, high-relevance backlink and a live distribution channel for the underlying data, which is exactly the kind of linkable asset link-builders say still works in 2026.
evidence: Link-building analysis for 2026 explicitly calls out that <cite index="32-2">Links earned through videos, infographics, podcasts, and utility tools/widgets are highly valuable, given the growing role of interactive assets</cite>, and separately that <cite index="33-1,33-2">One financial services company created a retirement planning calculator that earned over 1,200 backlinks in its first year with minimal outreach. ROI calculators, assessment quizzes, comparison engines, and industry-specific templates all perform extremely well.</cite> Real-estate-specific guidance adds that <cite index="35-1">The common thread is providing specific, locally-grounded, data-backed information that writers and journalists can reference with attribution.</cite>
notes:
effort: days
expected: 10-20 embeds placed on tenant-org, legal-aid, and local-news sites within 90 days, generating referring domains that move the domain-authority needle toward the 90%-search-share goal; track via backlink monitoring and referral traffic from embed domains.
first step: Build a single-address lookup widget (HTML iframe, no JS framework dependency) returning stabilization status + DHCR registration + violation count, then pitch it directly to 10 named NYC tenant-rights orgs and housing reporters already covered by the daily-brief outreach list.

name: One-time paid 'Building Report' (no subscription required)
hypothesis: Most visitors need this data exactly once — before signing a specific lease or making a specific offer — not on an ongoing basis, so a $4.99/mo recurring subscription is the wrong ask for the highest-intent moment. A one-time unlocked PDF/page report (ownership history, violations, DHCR registration, comparable rents) sold as a single purchase matches the actual use case, requires no re-engagement, and converts visitors who would never commit to a subscription with zero registered accounts today.
evidence: A comparable tenant-facing product in this exact space is already monetizing a single-use moment this way: <cite index="25-11,25-12,25-13">Is your landlord allowed to do that? Get a plain-English lease review with red flags and state-specific tenant rights. $9.99, one-time.</cite> This validates that renters will pay a small one-time fee at the decision point rather than commit to a subscription for information they need once.
notes:
effort: days
expected: First paid dollar on the site; target 50-100 one-time purchases/month at $7-9.99 within 90 days of launch, tracked via Stripe one-time checkout separate from the Plus subscription funnel.
first step: Pick 3 high-traffic building pages, add a 'Get the full building report' one-time-purchase button (Stripe Checkout, no account required) that unlocks owner/agent history, full violation timeline, and portfolio cross-reference as a downloadable PDF.
[2026-07-28] candidate→active: was live in production since 2026-07-27 (api_server.py Stripe checkout + building_reports table + lifecycle.py buyer sequence) but never flipped from candidate — same unfixed claim as gsc_integration. Confirmed by code before flipping.

name: Free-account onboarding sequence
hypothesis: A new account currently receives nothing at all, so the first impression after signing up is silence. A welcome, one activation nudge for people who never saved anything, and one lapsed check should raise the 6% week-over-week return rate.
evidence: Supabase auth runs with mailer_autoconfirm and no SMTP host: no confirmation and no welcome is sent. 17 of 20 accounts have never saved a building.
notes: Accounts created before the 2026-07-27 cutover never enter the sequence — gating only the welcome on age would still have fired the day-3 and day-21 steps at 17 cold accounts at once, which is the backfill blast the owner explicitly ruled out.
